evidence: M-O s.v. syrup, after Latham and Du Cange
terms.comment: The medieval word, from Arabic sharāb; classical Latin has only the syrups of boiled grape-must (sapa, dēfrutum), so it fills a real gap. The lexicon already uses it for cough syrup.

terms.gloss: must boiled down to a syrup
evidence: Plin. NH 14.80; Ov. F. 4.780; Mart. 7.53.6 (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The Romans’ own sweet syrup, from grape juice; the word for a home-made fruit syrup.
“Maple tears”: classical lacrima of the gum or sap that drips from a plant (Verg. G. 4.160; Plin. NH 11.14) and acernus, of maple.

phrases.latin: in summō habuimus cāseum mollem et sapam et cocleās singulās
phrases.english: to finish we had soft cheese and must-syrup and a snail each

sources: Lewis & Short: sapa · Lewis & Short: lacrima · Lewis & Short: acernus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. syrup, maple syrup, cough syrup.
Petronius from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-petronius).
